title: AST Wildlife Investigation: Lower Kalskag [AK25129043]

title: AST Failure To Salvage Moose: Farewell GMU 19C [AK25091599]
summary: On 09/08/2025, McGrath AWT contacted two hunters with a dead 52" bull moose at the Farewell Strip. Investigation determined Jeffery Harris, age 42 of Anchorage, took the moose on the evening of September 5th. The moose was left in the field for approximately 14 hours before being field dressed. Temperatures throughout the region were warm and wet. The meat of the moose spoiled due to not being properly cared for in a timely manner. Investigation also determined Harris took the two front shoulders, and other chunks of meat, and discarded them in the brush due to their putrid smell and colors. Harris was issued a citation for failing to salvage all edible meat. The moose rack and rotten meat were seized as evidence. Arraignment was set for October 9, 2025, in the Aniak Court.

summary: On 08/06/2024, William Patrick Lee Jr., age 58 of Olalla, Washington, was issued a summons to appear in Galena District Court on misdemeanor charges stemming from a 2024 moose hunt on the Nowitna River. Investigation revealed Lee was awarded the DM806 moose permit, an Alaska resident-only draw, and harvested a bull moose unlawfully. Additionally, Lee failed to purchase an appropriate non-resident license and tag and violated a permit hunt condition by failing to submit the lower jaw as required. Arraignment is scheduled for 08/28/2025 at 1430 hours.

title: AST Death Investigation: Anchorage [AK25067686]
summary: On July 11, 2025, at around 1:00 am, a fight occurred in a cell between two inmates at the Anchorage Correctional Center. Correctional Officers responded to the fight, and 53-year-old inmate Jeffrey Foreman became combative and charged officers who were giving commands to Foreman. Officers used force to put Foreman on the ground and began restraining him. While being restrained, Foreman kicked an officer and was placed in leg restraints. Shortly after he was restrained, Foreman became unresponsive, and lifesaving efforts were started immediately by correctional staff and later the Anchorage Fire Department. Despite these efforts, Foreman was declared deceased at the facility. His next of kin have been notified, and his body has been sent to the State Medical Examiner’s Office for autopsy.

title: AST Search and Rescue: Indian Valley Trail [AK25037053]
summary: Alaska State Troopers, in coordination with the Alaska Mountain Rescue Group (AMRG), successfully rescued a hiker in distress near the Indian Creek Trailhead late Saturday night. At approximately 11:22 PM on April 19, authorities received an SOS activation from a Garmin device belonging to a 52-year-old male hiking alone in the Indian Creek area. The hiker, who had undergone knee replacement surgery last October, was reported overdue by a companion waiting at the trailhead. The rescue operation proceeded despite a brief cancellation of the SOS call, as the hiker later reported he couldn't feel his feet. After midnight, the Alaska Mountain Rescue Group was deployed to the last known coordinates. At approximately 2:55 AM, rescuers made contact with the hiker about a mile from the parking lot
sourceAttribution: Source: Alaska State Troopers Daily Dispatch

The Wildlife Troopers acquired his coordinates (61.76298 N, 147.07162 W). They were located approximately one mile from the toe of the Nelchina glacier and down on the river. The Rescue Coordination Center was notified, and the Air National Guard launched a helicopter to assist with the rescue. At approximately 1825 hours, the helicopter was on the scene to extract the injured male. He was then transported to Providence Hospital, where he was treated for his injuries.
